121311234的意思是 “隐隐约约出现”“逼近”“即将来临”。例如：A storm is looming on the horizon.（一场暴风雨即将来临。）的中文意思是 “大喊；叫嚷；呼喊”。的中文意思是 “前任；前辈”。“concessions” 常见的中文释义为 “让步；特许；优惠”。的中文意思是 “激怒”“使大怒”。例如，他的行为激怒了父母。在这里表示泽连斯基总统拒绝做出那些让步的行为让特朗普非常生气。 的中文意思是 “被阻止”“被威慑”。在这段文本中，可以理解为如果普京不被阻止、不被威慑，乌克兰人认为他会违背任何结束战争的承诺。常见的中文释义为 “行凶抢劫；（尤指在公共场所）行凶抢劫未遂”。在这段文本中，“a planned political mugging” 可以理解为 “一场有计划的政治‘打劫’”，意味着一方对另一方采取了具有攻击性、强迫性的政治行动，就像在街头的抢劫行为一样，带有强行获取利益或迫使对方就范的意味。常见的中文释义为 “使突然发生；加速”。例如：The event precipitated a crisis.（这个事件引发了一场危机。）在给定的文本中，“or to precipitate a crisis that would allow them to blame him for whatever happens next” 可理解为 “或者引发一场危机，这场危机能让他们把接下来发生的任何事情都归咎于他”。常见的中文释义为 “松弛；懈怠；萧条”。在这句话中，“take up the slack” 可理解为 “承担（弥补）空缺、填补不足”。例如，当一个团队中的某个人离开后，其他人就要 “take up the slack”，承担起那个人原本的工作任务，以确保整个团队的工作不受影响。的中文意思是 “疯狂的；狂乱的；紧张忙乱的”。例如：He was in a frantic rush to finish the work.（他疯狂地赶工完成工作。）可以用来形容人在紧急情况下的慌乱状态，或者形容某个场景充满了紧张和混乱。的常见中文释义为 “摊牌；最后的一决胜负”。在这段文本中，“a tense and public showdown” 可以理解为一场紧张且公开的摊牌或对决。这里指乌克兰总统泽连斯基与特朗普和 JD Vance 之间发生了紧张的公开冲突。的意思是 “鲜明的对比”。可以用来描述两个事物在某个方面存在很大的差异。例如：The two paintings present a sharp contrast in style.（这两幅画在风格上呈现出鲜明的对比。）在给出的文本中，“a sharp contrast to the scenes in the Oval Office” 表示与在白宫椭圆形办公室的场景形成鲜明对比。的中文意思是 “联合；联盟；结合体”。在上述语境中，“coalition of the willing” 可理解为 “自愿联盟”，即欧洲各国领导人为了保卫乌克兰而形成的一个自愿参与的联合组织。的意思是 “缺乏的”“不足的”“稀少的”。例如：Food and water were scarce after the earthquake.（地震后食物和水很缺乏。）在给定的文本中 “but details of who would contribute what were scarce” 表示 “但是关于谁将贡献什么的细节是稀少的”。的意思是 “螺旋式上升或下降”“急剧变化”。在这个上下文中可以理解为 “急剧变化”，即椭圆形办公室的会议从欢笑状态急剧转变为愤怒状态。的中文意思是 “完全的；彻底的；直率的”。例如：“He gave an outright refusal.”（他断然拒绝。）在给定的文本中，“stopped short of an outright apology” 可以理解为 “没有做出完全的道歉”。常见的中文释义为 “适度的”“中等的”“温和的”。在这个语境中，“moderate Republican Nebraska Congressman Don Bacon” 可理解为 “温和的内布拉斯加州共和党众议员唐・培根”，这里的 “moderate” 用来修饰众议员的政治立场，即他的政治主张可能较为温和、不激进。的意思是 “显著的；值得注意的；著名的”。在这段文本中，“notable exceptions” 指的是那些引人注目的例外情况。例如，意大利的 Giorgia Meloni 和匈牙利的 Viktor Orban 与其他人不同，他们没有在社交媒体上支持泽连斯基，这种情况是显著的、值得注意的例外。常见的中文释义为 “具体的”“实在的”“有形的”。在这个句子中，“concrete action” 可以理解为 “具体的行动”，强调行动不是抽象的、模糊的，而是有实际内容、可以被明确感知和执行的行动。常用的中文意思有 “偶然发生的；依情况而定的；（军队等）分遣队，小分队”。
例如：The success of the plan is contingent on good weather.（这个计划的成功取决于良好的天气。）这里 “contingent on” 表示 “取决于……”，体现了 “依情况而定” 的含义。
再如：A contingent of soldiers was sent to the area.（一支小分队被派往那个地区。）这里 “contingent” 表示 “分遣队，小分队”。在这里是 “直言不讳的”“大声表达的” 意思。在这段文本中，“Poland – which has long been one of Kyiv's most vocal supporters” 指波兰一直是基辅最直言不讳的支持者之一，即波兰在支持乌克兰这件事上态度明确且积极表达自己的支持立场。表示 “淡化、贬低、对…… 轻描淡写”；“休战”“停战”“和解期间”。通常指冲突的各方同意在一定时间内停止敌对行动。例如，两国在激烈的战争后宣布进入一段时期的 truce，双方军队在此期间停止战斗，以便进行和平谈判或让民众得到暂时的安宁。假设、假说。在这段文本中，“Under the hypothesis” 表示 “在这个假设之下”，即对于法国提出的某个想法或方案的一种假定情况。在这里指法国提出的双方在空中、海上以及能源基础设施周围达成四周休战的这个设想情况。obsess” 的中文释义为 “使痴迷；使迷恋；使着迷”。例如：He is obsessed with computer games.（他痴迷于电脑游戏。）这个词通常用来形容人对某事物有着过度的、难以自拔的喜爱或关注。“prolong” 的中文意思是 “延长”“拉长”“拖延”。例如：prolong the meeting（延长会议）；prolong the deadline（延长截止日期）。这个词通常用于表示将时间、长度等方面进行扩展。常见的中文释义为 “倡议；新方案；主动性”。
例如，“The government has launched several initiatives to promote environmental protection.”（政府推出了几项倡议以促进环境保护。）这里的 “initiatives” 表示 “倡议”。“collectivity” 常见的中文释义为 “集体性；集体；集体主义”。
它可以指某个事物所具有的集体的特性，比如一个团队的行动展现出很强的 collectivity，就是说这个团队的行动具有高度的集体性。
“集体性” 强调事物作为一个整体所呈现出的特征，是多个个体组合在一起共同表现出的一种状态或性质。“集体” 则是一群人的组合，可以是一个组织、团体等。“集体主义” 是一种强调集体利益高于个人利益的观念和价值取向。

每日头条/20240408-is-the-world-heading-into-.title: 20240408-Is the world heading into recession
每日头条/20240408-is-the-world-heading-into-.description:
Open: Pasted image 20250408004813.png
US President Donald Trump's tariffs have ignited wildfires across global stock markets, but does that mean we are heading for a recession?The first thing to stress is that what happens in the stock market is not the same as what happens in the economy - falling share prices do not always mean economic misery ahead.But sometimes they do.Very large falls in stock market values, like these, mean there has been a fundamental reappraisal of future profits for the companies that make up the stock markets of the world.What markets quite reasonably expect is that increased tariffs will mean that costs will rise and profits will fall.That doesn't mean that a recession is inevitable but the chances are clearly much higher than they were before Trump announced the most severe and wide-ranging tariffs seen in a century.An economy is defined as being in recession when the total of everything we and the government spend or export shrinks for two successive three-month periods.Between October and December last year, the UK economy grew a tiny 0.1% and the latest monthly data showed it shrank by the same amount in January.The first estimate of how the UK economy fared in February will be released this coming Friday.So, we are a long way off being able to tell whether we have hit that definition.
FOLLOW LIVE: Markets continue to fall in tariff turmoil
Why Asian markets are seeing such steep falls
How do share price falls affect me? However, in the bloodbath of stock market falls, there are some particularly gory and worrying casualties.Banks are often seen as proxies for economies. As one well respected market watcher told me today: "The thing that made me catch my breath was the fall in the banks."HSBC and Standard Chartered - which operate at the intersection of international trade between east and west - were both down more than 10% overnight before recovering some ground.Other warning signs are not on stock markets but commodity exchanges.Copper and oil prices are considered barometers of global economic health.Both have fallen more than 15% since Trump dropped his tariff bombshell.There haven't been many truly global recessions.The 1930s, the aftermath of the Great Financial Crisis and the panic around the pandemic are three rare examples of when we saw synchronised downturns in major economies.It is still considered unlikely that we would see something on that scale this time but the chances of recession in the US, UK and European Union have been significantly upgraded by most economic analysts.On the plus side for UK Chancellor Rachel Reeves, the government's borrowing costs are likely to dip by around £5bn to £6bn a year as investors flock to the relative safety of government bonds.But that will be more than offset by hits to government tax receipts if and when the economy as a whole goes into reverse.

每日头条/20250220-trump-aide-tells-ukraine-t.title: 20250220-Trump aide tells Ukraine to 'tone down' US criticism as Russia warns against Nato troops
每日头条/20250220-trump-aide-tells-ukraine-t.description:
万斯称，在俄乌谈判中“一切都可以讨论”。 Image source,Getty Images Republican【共和党人】 Vice President JD Vance is speaking at the 2025 Conservative【保守的】 Political Action Conference (CPAC) in Washington and is being asked about US ties to Europe and the war in Ukraine. On Europe, Vance says the US will continue to have "important alliances", but the strength of the relationship depends on whether they take their "societies【社会】 in the right direction". On the war in Ukraine, Vance says President Donald Trump believes "everything is on the table"【一切都可以讨论】 when it comes to negotiations with Russia. Vance also defended【为…… 辩护】 Trump's call with Putin earlier this month, which sparked【引发；激起；触发】 a backlash【强烈反对】 in the US and around the world. "How are you going to end the war unless you talk to Russia?" Vance says. He adds that "peace is in the interest"【和平符合利益】 of the US and Europe and says Trump will "fight for it for the remainder【剩余任期】 of his administration".
Image source,Getty Images Image caption, In Kherson, a high-rise building collapsed after shelling On the ground in Ukraine, the war rages on, impacting thousands of lives both in Ukraine and Russia.【对乌克兰和俄罗斯的数千人的生活产生影响。】 Today, in Nikopol in the Dnipropetrovsk region, two men were killed and a woman was injured after Russian shelling【炮击；炮轰；轰炸等】, according to the regional governor Serhiy Lyask. Writing on Telegram, Lyask says a 39-year-old woman was injured during the strike and received medical assistance. Some 200km (124 miles) south, in Kherson, a high-rise building collapsed after Russian shelling, the head of the Kherson regional military administration says. Writing on Telegram, Oleksandr Prokudin says the body of one man was found under the rubble【瓦砾；碎石；碎砖】. And in the city of Kostyantynivka, which is situated【位于；坐落在】 in the Donetsk region, at least four people - two men and two women - have been killed as a result of four airstrikes and artillery【火炮；大炮；炮兵部队】 shelling, according to the regional head Vadym Filashkin. In a post on Telegram, Filashkin details the destruction, which includes seven homes, four apartment buildings, three power lines, and a gas pipeline. A strike in the same city yesterday resulted in the death of two people, according to Filashkin.
乌克兰寄希望于美国会议 James Waterhouse Reporting from Kyiv US special envoy Keith Kellogg is now meeting with Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky, an interaction on which Ukraine will be pinning its hopes. In a break from the norm【常态】, officials here are keen【渴望的；热衷于；热切的；敏锐的】 to give Kellogg what they call a “full picture” of the war, including a trip to the frontline – unheard of on official visits. Kellogg's sole【唯一的；仅有的；单独的】 job is to liaise【联络；联系；协调】 with Ukraine and maintain a two-way channel of communication. All officials have heard from the US side so far is what has come from his boss across the Atlantic. And looking at Kellogg’s lack of involvement in the Riyadh talks between Russia and the US, it's clear more senior people, such as Secretary of State Marco Rubio, are handling the negotiations. What will be crucial is how well Kellogg can relay【传达；传递】 what he hears here, and how important his perception【看法；认知；洞察力】 of the US's continued military support is. What is a more worrying equation for Kyiv is the structure of Russia-US talks continuing, with perhaps a more peripheral【边缘的；次要的；外围的】 American representative liaising with Ukraine's president. Zelensky is now fighting even harder to get involved in the peace talks – a feat【功绩；壮举；技艺表演】 made much more difficult by Trump questioning his democratically elected integrity. 泽连斯基现在正更加努力地参与和平谈判——特朗普质疑他民主选举的诚信，这一壮举变得更加困难。
克里姆林宫称泽连斯基的特朗普言论 “不可接受” Image source,Reuters Earlier today, Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov called Volodymr Zelensky's comments "inadmissible", following the heated【激烈的；热烈的；加热的】 rift【裂痕；分歧】 between the US and Ukraine presidents. "Often, representatives【代表】 of the Ukrainian regime, especially in recent months, allow themselves to make completely inadmissible statements about the heads of other states," Peskov says. Zelensky said on Wednesday that the US president is "living in a disinformation space" governed by Moscow. The Ukrainian president also rejected Trump's claims that his approval ratings are very low, as well as suggestions that Ukraine has been spending US aid in a non-transparent【不透明的；非透明的】 way. That's a wrap【包裹；完成；总结】 on our experts answering your questions about the Ukraine war and latest diplomatic row on how to achieve peace. If you missed it, you can scroll back on our stream at the top of the page to 14:30 to catch the session. Our team of correspondents and reporters will be back tomorrow for another round of Q&As, and we want to hear what questions you have for them.
凯洛格和泽连斯基仍在基辅举行会谈。 Image source,Reuters We've just received an image of US Special Envoy to Ukraine Keith Kellogg and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky speaking together. Moments ago we heard that a planned joint【联合】 press【新闻发布会；按下；压；挤；逼迫。】 conference【新闻发布会；按下；压；挤；逼迫。】 had been cancelled - cameras were briefly【短暂地】 let in【准许进入；让……进来】 before being ushered out【被引领出去；被引导出去；被带出去。具体的意思需要结合上下文语境，这里暂译为 “被引领出去”。这里的 “ushered” 在这个句子中表示的是摄像机被引导着出去，即 “被引领出去”。】. The pair are currently in talks, though it's unclear right now when and how we will be updated on how the discussions have gone.
万斯表示，战争对俄罗斯和乌克兰不利 —— 但 “最重要的是对美国不利”。 Image source,Getty Images We can now bring you some comments from US Vice President JD Vance, who says that Washington believes the ongoing war is not only bad for Russia, Ukraine and Europe, but "most importantly, it is bad for the United States". In a post on X, Vance says that he and President Trump have repeatedly said for the past three years that the war "wouldn't have started" if Trump had been in office - instead of former US President Joe Biden. He says that Trump is "dealing with reality" and "facts", which include, in his view, that the US retains【保留】 "substantial【巨大的；大量的；重大的。】 leverage【影响力；杠杆作用】 over both parties to the conflict".【“对冲突双方都有很大的影响力”。】 We'll be hearing from Vance himself shortly, when he addresses the Conservative Political Action Conference (CPAC).
泽连斯基 - 凯洛格新闻发布会取消。 James Waterhouse Reporting from Kyiv A planned press conference with Ukrainian President Zelensky and the US Chief Envoy to Ukraine Keith Kellogg has been cancelled. Cameras were briefly let in before being ushered out. The pair are currently in talks - the BBC understands it was a format imposed by the Americans, with a Ukrainian sources telling the BBC that Kellogg appears increasingly “sidelined”【边缘化】 by the Trump administration. 两人目前正在谈判 —— 英国广播公司理解这是美国人强加的一种形式，乌克兰消息来源告诉英国广播公司，凯洛格似乎越来越被特朗普政府 “边缘化”。 They added that Zelensky is “motivated” by the events of recent days. 美国向乌克兰提供的矿产交易是什么？ Earlier today, White House National Security Adviser Michael Waltz [said that Ukraine needs to "take a hard look and sign that deal"] That deal he's referring to was proposed by US President Trump in a statement on 3 February. In the deal, Ukraine would supply the US with rare earth minerals as a form of payment for Washington's financial support. The deal also suggests the minerals could be compensation【补偿；赔偿；报酬】 for the aid the US has already provided to Ukraine since Russia invaded in 2022. But Zelensky publicly rejected this bid【出价；投标；报价】 from Trump, claiming that it is not "a serious conversation and that he "cannot sell our state". Though the deal remains unsigned, [Trump has accused Zelensky of "breaking the deal".] Whilst【然；然而；当…… 的时候】 few have criticised it, many [Ukrainian commentators have generally hailed Donald Trump's proposal]
朔尔茨：“通过暴力改变边界是不被允许的。” Image source,Reuters Germany is days away from a general election and Chancellor Olaf Scholz has spoken about Ukraine in a speech on the election trail in the town of Ilsede, Lower Saxony. A two-hour flight away, there's a war happening, the chancellor says, adding that in no uncertain terms: "Russia has invaded Ukraine". "Even with the new American government, we will focus on and give it our all to secure an independent, sovereign and democratic future for Ukraine," he says. Addressing comments【回应评论】 by President Trump about Ukraine's leader being a "dictator", Scholz says "we cannot start doubting the political will of the Ukrainian citizen - they have elected the current president". The German leader says supporting Ukraine should not be boiled down【浓缩，归结为】 as a business decision, dismissing a US plan to take Ukraine's minerals in exchange for the support it has given to Kyiv. "It is not about raw【未加工的；生的；原始的；】 materials," he says, "it is about the fact that we cannot accept that an imperial wish leads to a country having to give away territory". “这是关于我们不能接受一个帝国的愿望导致一个国家不得不割让领土这一事实。” "We keep the principle we agreed together in Europe, moving borders through violence is not allowed and that we have to respect and accept borders." We're now starting a Q&A on the war in Ukraine in the livestream at the top of this page, with your questions answered by BBC experts. You can watch along by clicking the Watch live button above. Share
泽伦斯基正在做丘吉尔为英国做的事情 —— 英国国防大臣 We've just been hearing from the UK's Defence Secretary John Healey, who is currently on a trip to Norway after the countries [reached a new agreement on defence] "This war started because Russia invaded the territory of a sovereign state," he says. "This war could be ended today, if President Putin withdrew his troops from Ukraine." Trump recently drew criticism for calling Zelensky a "dictator", but Healey stands firm in his defence of the Ukrainian president. Healey describes how, in his second day in the role, he flew to meet Zelensky and saw the leader's "commitment to his country". "He's the elected leader in Ukraine, and he's done what Winston Churchill did in Britain in the Second World War; suspended【暂停的】 elections while at war," he says. "Our job is to stand with the Ukrainians, support the Ukrainians, support them in their fight. And if they choose to talk, support them in the negotiations as well. "It's in President Trump and America's interests that we get a durable peace."
白宫安全顾问称，基辅需要控制对美国的批评 Image source,Reuters White House National Security Adviser Michael Waltz says Ukraine needs to rein in its criticism of the US, as Washington tries to secure a peace deal to end the war. "It's unacceptable, they [Ukraine] need to tone it down【语气缓和一些】 and take a hard look and sign that deal," he tells Fox News. The deal he is referring to is a push by Donald Trump for access to rare minerals in Ukraine in return for aid, or even as compensation for the support the US has already provided. "We presented the Ukrainians really an incredible, and a historic opportunity," the adviser says, adding that it would be "sustainable" and "the best" security guarantee they could hope for. Zelensky has publicly rejected an American bid to gain access to – and profit from - Ukrainian minerals, saying: "I can't sell our state." But he says that the two countries can reconcile their differences.
乌克兰人希望对特朗普的说法做出回应。 Abdujalil Abdurasulov Reporting from Kyiv People here are shocked and outraged【愤怒】 and extremely worried about the growing rift between US President Donald Trump and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky because it doesn’t bring anything good for Ukraine. People are saying Ukraine must respond to the false claims Trump is making. Those claims are strikingly similar to what people hear from Moscow. Ukrainians are saying Zelensky is certainly not a dictator and his ratings are much higher than 4%, as Trump suggested. According to the latest polls【民意调查】, around 57% of the population support Zelensky. Trump repeatedly claims that Zelensky refuses to hold elections in the country. However, elections at a time of martial【军事管制时期的；战争的；军事的】 law are banned in Ukraine. Logistically【从后勤方面来说；在后勤方面】, it’s not possible to hold them while hostilities are continuing. How would military personnel vote? What about those under occupation or people who have had to flee the country? If you disregard these people, can you call these elections democratic?
Read more from BBC Verify's fact-checking on Trump's claims 英国和挪威加强联合防御以对抗俄罗斯。 We've just seen a joint statement between the UK and Norway, where both nations have expressed their "ironclad"【坚如磐石的；不可动摇的】 and "unwavering" 【坚定不移的】support for Ukraine and pledged【承诺；保证】 to enhance their own defence. The countries say they are committing to enhancing their "critical undersea infrastructure" as "Russia's aggression across Europe" continues "growing". They also say they will increase intelligence co-operation and enhance co-operation in the High North and North Atlantic - as sea is where the UK and Norway share "the closest bonds".【最紧密的联系】 "We recognise that Russia is willing to use all means at its disposal【处置；处理；清除；销毁；扔掉。这里可以结合上下文翻译为 “使用其所能使用的一切手段” 中的 “手段”。最终答案：手段。】 to undermine【破坏；逐渐削弱】 European cohesion【凝聚力；内聚力；黏合力。】 and support to Ukraine," the statement reads. For context, the UK and Norway describe themselves as "the closest of Allies", with a "deep history", having a "common outlook", and "commitment【承诺；保证；致力；献身；承担义务。】 to democracy". Both countries will use the coming months to work towards a new defence agreement, hoping to sign it by the summer.
照片：乌克兰人向 “天堂百人” 致敬。 As we mentioned in our previous post, Ukrainians are paying tribute to pro-democracy demonstrators who were killed more than 11 years ago during protests against the then pro-Russian president Viktor Yanukovych. Here's a look at a memorial event in the capital, Kyiv: Image source,EPA-EFE/REX/Shutterstock Image source,EPA-EFE/REX/Shutterstock Image source,EPA-EFE/REX/Shutterstock
乌克兰在与俄罗斯的战争持续之际纪念 “天堂百人”。 Vitaliy Shevchenko
BBC Monitoring's Russia editor Today, Ukraine is holding memorial events recalling something that happened more than 11 years ago but has everything to do with what is going on today. Ukraine is honouring【纪念；向…… 致敬】 "The Heavenly Hundred" – pro-democracy demonstrators killed during protests against the then pro-Russian president Viktor Yanukovych in late 2013 to early 2014. These protests led to Yanukovych fleeing to Russia before Russia secretly sent troops to Ukraine in 2014 and ultimately launched an open, full-scale invasion in 2022. Now, President Volodymyr Zelensky has posted a video of himself and his wife Olena paying their respects at a monument in central Kyiv. "Heroes who died defending freedom, dignity【尊严】 and our country’s right to choose its own future freely. It’s a sacrifice that reminds us of the price of self-determination," President Zelensky says. Russia views the protests as a Western-sponsored【西方资助的】 coup. Image source,EPA Image caption, Ukrainians are today paying tribute to those killed in protests against a former pro-Russian leader
“乌克兰是一个民主国家，而普京领导的俄罗斯不是。”—— 欧盟 Image source,Getty Images The European Union has responded to US President Donald Trump's accusation【指责；控告；谴责】 from the previous day, when he called Zelensky a "dictator". "Ukraine is a democracy, [President Vladimir] Putin's Russia is not," says EU spokesman Stefan de Keersmaecker. He adds that the EU has a "straightforward【直截了当的；简单明了的】 and clear position" on the matter, saying, "President Zelensky was legitimately【合法地；正当地】 elected in free, fair and democratic elections". The EU is a key ally of Ukraine, even though the country is not a member state.
乌克兰外交部长表示，他与美国特使讨论了 “公正持久的和平”。 Image source,Andrii Sybiha Image caption, Ukraine's Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha (L) meets Keith Kellogg, Trump's Ukraine envoy, in Kyiv Ukraine's foreign affairs minister says he discussed ways towards achieving a "comprehensive【全面的；综合的；广泛的；包罗万象的。】, just, and lasting peace" in Ukraine with Keith Kellogg, Trump's Ukraine envoy who is in Kyiv. In a post on X, Andrii Sybiha says: "I affirmed Ukraine's willingness to achieve peace through strength and our vision for the necessary steps. I also reiterated【重申】 that the security of Ukraine and the transatlantic【跨大西洋的】 is indivisible【不可分割的】." Kellogg is expected to meet Ukraine's President Zelensky later today. We'll let you know as soon as we have more details.
乌克兰情报部门负责人预计 “今年” 停火。 Vitaliy Shevchenko
BBC Monitoring's Russia editor Image source,Reuters Kyrylo Budanov, the head of Ukraine’s military intelligence HUR, believes Ukraine and Russia are likely to strike【发动打击；达成停火协议 这里的 “strike” 有两种含义，根据上下文可知应取 “达成（协议）” 之意。翻译为 “达成”。】 a ceasefire deal by the end of this year. “I think we’ll reach a ceasefire regime【政权；制度；管理体制。在给定的上下文中，可翻译为 “停火制度”。】 this year. How long it will last or how effective it will be is another matter,” Budanov says in an interview, external. “Most components” are in place for a ceasefire agreement to be concluded this year, he says. But he adds that he is sceptical【持怀疑态度的】 about the effectiveness of any peacekeeping force that may be deployed to Ukraine. “Show me at least one country in the world where deploying peacekeepers worked,” he says.

每日头条/20250222-'trump-hasn't-got-any-plan.title: 20250222-'Trump hasn't got any plan' Russians speak to BBC after three years of war
每日头条/20250222-'trump-hasn't-got-any-plan.description:
“特朗普没有任何计划”，战争三年后俄罗斯人接受英国广播公司采访时说道。 Open: Pasted image 20250223005353.png
Recruitment【招募】 posters【海报】 for the invasion of Ukraine are everywhere in RussiaDriving into Tver, the first thing I notice are the soldiers.They're everywhere. On billboards【广告牌】, the sides of buildings, at bus stops. Portraits with the words "Hero of Russia". Posters of troops with Kalashnikov rifles encouraging the public to "Love, be proud of and defend" Russia.In other words, to sign up【注册】 and go and fight in Ukraine. Three years after its full-scale invasion of its neighbour, Russia is seeking new recruits.Despite all the military imagery【军事意象；军事形象；战争景象等】 around town, if you live in Tver it's possible to convince yourself that life is normal. The front line is hundreds of miles away."Just look around," Mikhail, a local teacher, tells me. "Cars are passing by and all the shops are open. No shells are falling from anywhere. We are not panicking. We can't hear any sirens【警报声】 wailing【警报声哀号着；警报声长鸣着；警报声呼啸着。】. We do not run to any evacuation【疏散；撤离】 points."For many Russians their invasion of Ukraine – what the Kremlin still calls a "special military operation" – is something they only encounter on their TV screens.But for people like Anna, it's much more real.
Some people Anna knew never came back from fighting in Ukraine"I know a lot of people who went off to fight," Anna says when we get chatting on the street."Some of them never came home. I hope [the war] ends as soon as possible."Donald Trump claims that's what he wants, too. Without inviting Ukraine to the negotiating table, the Trump administration has already entered direct talks with the Russian leadership.What do Russians make of the US president and his overtures【提议；主动表示；姿态】 to Moscow?【“overtures” 常见的中文释义为 “提议；主动表示；姿态”。例如：His overtures for peace were well received.（他的和平提议受到了好评。）在这句话中，“overtures” 表示 “提议”，强调某人主动提出的关于和平的建议或主张。再比如：Her overtures of friendship were ignored.（她的友好姿态被忽视了。）这里 “overtures” 表示 “姿态”，即表达友好的一种行为表现。总的来说，“overtures” 通常用来描述某人主动做出的积极行动或表示，以达到某种目的，如建立关系、达成协议等。】"Trump is a dark horse," believes Anna. "I'm not sure what to expect from him."Some of the people I talk to in Tver repeat the official narrative they have been hearing for the last three years on state TV: that their country is not the aggressor, that Russia is defending Russians and Russian-speakers in Ukraine and liberating, not occupying, territory.It doesn't mean that Russian society as a whole buys into this alternative reality. 这并不意味着俄罗斯社会作为一个整体接受了这种替代现实。"In a society people always prefer to be in the mainstream," believes Andrei Kolesnikov, a columnist【专栏作家】 for newtimes.ru and Novaya Gazeta. "If the mainstream is pro-war and the TV says that we are at war with the West, the average citizen will think like this. It's easier not to think about the details. You want to live peacefully, so why not join the majority?
"Some researchers call this the foetal【胎儿的；胎的；似胎儿的；未出生的；处于胚胎状态的；未成熟的；幼稚的；软弱无力的；易受影响的；顺从的；】 position. When you defend yourself from this unexplainable world you look like a baby. You say: 'I can't explain to myself what is happening. I believe you. You can feed me with words. I'll accept it.' This is typical for all societies of this kind: a bit [1]authoritarian【专制的；独裁的；威权主义的。】, a bit totalitarian."【专制的；独裁的；极权主义的。】Larissa and her husband Valery willingly accept the official line."We're all for the special military operation," Larissa tells me. "We're ready to volunteer and go there ourselves!"They haven't yet, clearly."We hope [Russia] will be victorious. We want Ukraine's total capitulation."The police turn up. They've received a call informing them that "suspicious-looking people with a camera" are going around Tver. Meaning us.
Russian police asked the BBC about their reporting in TverThey're polite but want to know why we're here. They take a statement from our driver. They check our vehicle. They ask me for an official explanation for our visit. I tell them we're gauging【估量；评估；判断】 the mood【情绪；心情；心境；氛围；语气；】 away from Moscow. We show our documents, which are in order.【整齐有序；状况良好】
While we've been talking to the officers, a camera crew【摄制组；全体船员；工作人员】 from Russian state TV has [2]pitched【出现；到来；到达；抵达；（尤指）迅速地从一处移动到另一处；（尤指）突然来到，冒出，出现；（尤指）迅速地从一处移动到另一处；】 up and started filming【拍摄；摄制】 us."We were just passing," says the reporter, "and we spotted【发现；看到；注意到；认出；弄脏；弄上斑点；用点装饰；使有污点；使有斑驳；散布；】 the police and recognised you. Can you tell me what's going on?""I don't know," I reply. "Perhaps you can tell us?""What have you been filming?""We've been talking to people on the street," I say. "I believe we're allowed to do that.""Yes, in our country we have freedom of speech," the reporter replies. "Perhaps the police just want to help you? It's unpleasant to hear Western TV spreading fake news that there's no free speech in Russia. You're talking to people freely and no one gets in your way.""Apart from you," I point out. "And the police officers standing next to our car."
Russian state TV also interviewed the BBC about what they were doingThe incident【事件】, which lasted about an hour, is no real surprise. Three years of war have fuelled suspicion of the West inside Russia. Early signs of a thaw【解冻；缓和；变得温和】 in US-Russian relations have yet to change that.From talking to people in Tver it becomes clear that Russians are hoping that an end to the fighting will bring economic relief."Prices are so high now for the things I need most," says Yulia as she rocks her baby to sleep in a pram【婴儿车】. "Like the price of potatoes and onions. I really feel it."But teacher Mikhail doesn't feel that Donald Trump has any strategy for securing peace."Unfortunately, Trump hasn't got any plan," believes Mikhail. "He is an improviser.【improviser（即兴表演者；临时凑合者）】 He doesn't know what he's going to do. My sympathies【同情；慰问】 are with him. I'm glad he won. But speaking about this episode, we're all in the dark. And Trump is in the dark himself."
“authoritarian”和“totalitarian”在英语中都与权力的集中和强制有关，但它们之间存在一些细微的区别： ### 含义侧重 - authoritarian：通常用来形容一种强调权威、服从和等级制度的体系或人物。这种体系或人物倾向于要求他人绝对服从其命令和决定，权力往往集中在少数人或一个人手中，但不一定对社会生活的各个方面进行全面的控制。比如，一个公司的老板可能管理风格比较“authoritarian”，他会严格要求员工服从他的决策，但不会过多干涉员工的私人生活和工作以外的事情。 - totalitarian：更加强调对整个社会和个人生活的全面、彻底的控制。极权主义政权试图控制人们生活的方方面面，包括政治、经济、文化、思想、宗教等，不允许任何形式的独立思考和反对意见，追求对社会的绝对统治。如纳粹德国和法西斯意大利，政府对社会的一切都进行严格管控，人们几乎没有任何自由和权利。 ### 控制程度 - authoritarian：控制程度相对较低，主要集中在政治和公共事务等领域，在一定程度上允许社会存在一些私人空间和一定的多样性。例如，一些传统的威权国家，在政治上实行威权统治，但在经济和文化的某些方面还是有一定的自由发展空间。 - totalitarian：控制程度极高，试图消除社会中的一切异质性和多样性，将所有的社会资源和个人行为都纳入到国家的严格控制之下，个人完全服从于国家和政权。 ### 意识形态色彩 - authoritarian：不一定有强烈的、系统的意识形态作为支撑，更多的是基于统治者或统治集团的权力欲望和对秩序的追求来行使权力。 - totalitarian：往往与特定的极端意识形态紧密相连，如纳粹主义、共产主义的极端扭曲形式等，通过宣传和洗脑等手段，使民众接受并服从其意识形态，以实现对社会的全面控制。 ### 举例 - authoritarian：“The authoritarian leader made all the decisions without consulting the public.”（这位威权领导人在不征求公众意见的情况下做出了所有决定。） - totalitarian：“The totalitarian regime imposed strict censorship on all forms of media.”（极权政权对所有形式的媒体实施了严格的审查制度。）↩︎
“pitch up”有以下几种常见的含义及用法： 1. 到达；露面：通常用于口语中，指到达某个地方，有时带有一种突然或意外出现的感觉。例如：We were worried when he didn't pitch up on time.（他没有按时露面，我们很担心。）She finally pitched up at the party at midnight.（她最终在午夜时分出现在聚会上。） 2. 使（声音、音调等）升高：常用来描述声音、乐器音调等的升高。例如：The singer pitched up the final note for a dramatic effect.（歌手为了达到戏剧性的效果把最后一个音的音调升高了。）The radio signal suddenly pitched up, making it hard to understand the message.（无线电信号的音调突然升高，使得信息很难听清。） 3. 搭起（帐篷等）：与“pitch a tent”（搭帐篷）这个短语相关，“pitch up”更加强调动作的过程或开始搭建的动作。例如：They pitched up their tents by the river and started a campfire.（他们在河边搭起帐篷，生起了篝火。）We need to find a good spot to pitch up before it gets dark.（我们需要在天黑前找个好地方搭帐篷。） 4. （车辆等）颠簸着前进：用于描述车辆在不平整的道路等表面上颠簸行驶的状态。例如：The old jeep pitched up and down on the rough mountain road.（那辆旧吉普车在崎岖的山路上颠簸着前进。）The boat pitched up and down in the rough sea.（船在汹涌的海浪中上下颠簸。）↩︎

每日头条/20250223-germans-vote-in-high-stake.title: 20250223-Germans vote in high-stakes election watched closely by Europe and US
每日头条/20250223-germans-vote-in-high-stake.description:
德国人在一场受到欧洲和美国密切关注的高风险选举中投票。 stakes 重大利害关系；风险；赌注；股权等（具体含义需根据上下文确定）。这里结合上下文可翻译为 “重大利害关系”。 德国人在一场受到欧洲和美国密切关注的具有重大利害关系的选举中进行投票。因此这里可翻译为 “重大利害关系”。 Europe digital editor in BerlinReutersFrontrunner Friedrich Merz (2nd from R) mops his brow【额头】 at his last campaign event in Munich Frontrunner【领先者】 mops【擦汗（此处不太确定是动词 “擦汗” 还是名词 “擦汗的动作” 或 “擦汗用的东西”，需结合具体语境确定）注：仅根据给出的上下文猜测 “mops” 可能是 “mop（擦，抹）” 的第三人称单数形式或某种与擦汗相关的名词，因无更多信息，只能做此不太确定的翻译。如果上下文还有其他信息可进一步调整翻译。】Germans go to the polls【投票】 on Sunday, after an intense election campaign dominated by their country's faltering【摇摇欲坠的】 economy and a succession of deadly attacks that have made migration and security a focal issue. focal【焦点的；关键的；重要的。在给定的上下文中可翻译为 “关键的”。】Friedrich Merz, the 69-year-old conservative leader, is in pole-position to become Germany's next chancellor, in a vote closely watched in Europe and the US.pole【pole 的中文释义为 “杆；极点；电极” 等。在给定的上下文中，pole 的意思是 “领先的”。例如，这个公司在技术创新方面是 pole 的，即这个公司在技术创新方面是领先的。】 chancellor【总理；首相；（德国）财政大臣。（根据上下文语境，这里应为 “德国总理” 之意）】He promises to fix most problems in four years - a tall order for Europe's biggest economy and a creaking infrastructure.“tall order” 【的中文意思是 “艰巨的任务；苛求；高要求”。在这个句子中，“He promises to fix most problems in four years - a tall order for Europe's biggest economy and a creaking infrastructure.” 表示他承诺在四年内解决大部分问题，这对于欧洲最大的经济体以及老化的基础设施来说是一项艰巨的任务。】 creaking：【“creaking” 的意思是 “嘎吱作响的”“发出嘎吱声的”。在这个上下文中，“a creaking infrastructure” 指的是破旧不堪、摇摇欲坠且会发出嘎吱声响般的基础设施，形容基础设施状况很差，老旧且存在很多问题。】If Merz's Christian Democrats (CDU) win, he will need to forge an alliance with at least one other party, most likely Olaf Scholz's Social Democrats, whose government collapsed late last year.forge【” 常见的中文释义为 “锻造；伪造；稳步前进；建立（联盟等）”。在这个上下文中，“forge an alliance” 可理解为 “建立联盟”。也就是说，如果梅尔茨领导的基督教民主联盟获胜，他就需要与至少一个其他政党建立联盟，极有可能是与奥拉夫・朔尔茨领导的社会民主党建立联盟。这里强调了在特定政治情境下，通过努力达成合作关系、构建联盟的动作。】On the eve of the vote, Merz was adamant there would be no deal with the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD), which is poised to become the second biggest political force, ahead of Scholz's centre left.“adamant” 【的中文意思是 “坚决的”“坚定不移的”。在这段文本中，“Merz was adamant there would be no deal with the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD)” 可以理解为 “默茨坚决表示不会与极右翼的德国选择党达成任何协议”。这个词强调了说话者的态度非常坚决，没有任何商量的余地。】 “poised” 【在这里的意思是 “准备好的、蓄势待发的”。在这句话中，“which is poised to become the second biggest political force” 表示 “（德国选择党）即将成为第二大政治力量，处于准备就绪的状态”。】Some 59.2 million Germans are eligible to vote, and while millions already have by post, polls indicate as many 20% were undecided ahead of election day.The polls open at 08:00 (07:00 GMT) and close at 18:00, with a clear idea of a result during the evening.Voters are energised by this pivotal election, and campaigning continued right through Saturday evening with a final debate on national TV - the ninth this month.“energised” 【的中文意思是 “充满活力的”“被激励的”“被激发的”。在给定的文本中，“Voters are energised by this pivotal election” 表示选民们因这场关键的选举而充满活力、被激励起来。】 “pivotal” 的中文意思是 “关键的；至关重要的”。This is a watershed moment as Germany will have to make big decisions on the world stage as well as home. 【“watershed” 常见的中文释义为 “分水岭；转折点；重要关头”。在这句话中，“This is a watershed moment as Germany will have to make big decisions on the world stage as well as home.” 可理解为 “这是一个重要关头，因为德国将不得不在世界舞台以及国内做出重大决策”，强调这是一个具有重大意义的时刻，局势可能会发生重大变化。】Merz promises strong leadership in Europe, but Berlin is also under pressure to loosen the budget strings for its military.As Ukraine's second-biggest provider of military aid, Germany's next new government will face a US president who has condemned President Volodymyr Zelensky as a dictator and fractured the West's united front against Russia.“fractured” 【的意思是 “破裂、断裂”。在这个句子中，“fractured the West's united front against Russia” 可以理解为 “破坏了西方针对俄罗斯的统一战线”。】German political leaders have also been shocked by US Vice-President JD Vance, who has met the AfD's candidate for chancellor, Alice Weidel, and called for an end to the long-standing taboo of talking to the far right.“taboo” 【的中文意思是 “禁忌；忌讳”。在给定的文本中，“long-standing taboo” 表示长期以来的禁忌，即与极右翼进行交谈在过去一直是被视为禁忌的事情。】In Germany, that taboo is known as a firewall or brandmauer.Merz was accused of breaking it last month when he used their support in parliament. Several German cities saw protests against the far-right on Saturday.
Getty ImagesTwenty-five thousand people marched through the centre of Freiburg im Breisgau to protest against the far rightThe AfD is already popular in several eastern states, but it is rapidly growing in the west too, attracting support among younger Germans via TikTok.One Weidel campaign video has had four million views.Her message is simple: Vote AfD, break the firewall and change German politics.The AfD wants to leave the EU, scrap climate change measures, build nuclear power plants and repair gas lines and relations with Russia.But its voice has been loudest on migration and security after five deadly attacks since last May, including three during the election campaign in Magdeburg, Aschaffenburg and Munich - and all allegedly carried out by immigrants.A stabbing at Berlin's Holocaust memorial on Friday night has kept the issue in the headlines. The victim survived, and police said the attacker was Syrian and his motive antisemitic.stabbing” 【的意思是 “刺、戳、捅”，通常指用尖锐的物体进行攻击的行为。在给定的文本中，“A stabbing at Berlin's Holocaust memorial on Friday night” 表示周五晚上在柏林大屠杀纪念馆发生了一起刺伤事件。】 antisemitic” 的意思是 “反犹的”“反犹太人的”。 “motive” 常见的中文释义为 “动机；目的”。The AfD has embraced a highly controversial policy called "remigration", which it defines as deporting migrants who have committed crimes. But the term can also refer to the mass deportations of migrants and their descendants.controversial：有争议的。 “deporting” 的中文意思是 “驱逐”“递解出境”。 后代；后裔。在这段文本中，“migrants and their descendants” 指的是移民及其后代。
Getty ImagesPro-AfD supporters campaigned for their party in Berlin on the eve of the voteThe anti-immigration party has already secured a foothold in parts of the west, especially in Germany's old industrial heartland in the Ruhr valley.“foothold” 常见的中文释义为 “立足处；据点”。 industrial” 常见的中文意思是 “工业的；产业的”。In last summer's European elections it won the vote in some northern areas of the city of Duisburg, with 20% in Marxloh, 25% in an adjacent area and 30% next door to that.Marxloh is a vibrant district with a large immigrant community, known for its array of shops selling Turkish fashionwear for brides.“vibrant” 的意思是充满活力的、生机勃勃的。 fashionwear 时尚服饰。
Marxloh still has a functioning steelworks but much of the old coal and steel industry has goneBut it has also suffered extensively from the decline of the coal and steel industry and a lack of government investment.“extensively” 的中文意思是 “广阔地；广大地；广泛地”。In a park close to Marxloh's remaining steelworks, five young men in their early 20s explained why they all planned to vote AfD."We're young, we need work and they don't give us a chance to find training," one man complained."We've no money; everything's more expensive; there aren't many jobs any more and there's so much dirt here."
A short distance from Marxloh's remaining steelworks, young men like Viktor complain there are no jobs or training on offerThe AfD are not known for their social policies, but their message on security cuts through, and this group does not see the anti-immigration party as extreme."No, they're just normal people."In the east it is in the rural areas that the AfD does best, but in the west it is growing in cities that have lost their industrial base, says Prof Conrad Ziller of the University of Duisburg-Essen."Voices of people in favour of the AfD have become so loud, so if you're in a doctor's waiting room it's really common to hear people chat about getting angry about the established politicians and government."Migration is the most common frustration, and he believes Weidel has capitalised on that by appearing so prominently in all the TV debates.“capitalised” 在这句话中的意思是 “利用；从…… 中获利”。 “prominently” 的中文意思是 “显著地；突出地”。Often when the debate touched on the economy, social justice or inequality, Prof Ziller said "the AfD deflected it and said the main problem is not economics, it's migration, and the government didn't do a good job".inequality 不平等、不均衡。 “deflected” 的意思是 “转移、引开、使转向”While the opinion polls have been consistent about who is leading the race, some of the parties might not make it over the 5% threshold for the newly slimmed-down parliament.“consistent” 的中文意思是 “一致的”“始终如一的”。 “threshold” 常见的中文释义为 “门槛”“阈值”“界限” “slimmed-down” 的字面意思是 “精简的、瘦身的”。 “parliament” 常见的中文释义为 “议会”“国会”The fewer parties that make it into the the 630-seat Bundestag, the more straightforward it will be to form a coalition with a majority.“straightforward” 的中文意思是 “简单的”“直接的”“易懂的”。 “coalition” 的中文意思是 “联合；联盟；结合体”。 “majority” 的中文意思是 “多数；大多数；多数党；多数派”。The economic liberals, the Free Democratic Party (FDP), were in the outgoing government but they risk oblivion on Sunday along with left-wing populist party BSW.“liberals” 常见的中文释义为 “自由主义者”。 “outgoing” 常见的中文意思是 “即将离职的”“即将卸任的”。 “oblivion” 常见的中文释义为 “遗忘；湮没；无意识状态”。 “populist” 的中文意思是 “民粹主义的；平民主义的”。The Left party, however, has seen a resurgence in recent days and pollsters suggest it will become the fifth largest party after the Greens.“resurgence” 的中文意思是 “复苏”“复兴”“再次兴起”。 pollsters 民意调查者。

每日头条/20250224-new-german-leader-signals-.title: 20250224-New German leader signals seismic shift in transatlantic relations
每日头条/20250224-new-german-leader-signals-.description:
德国新领导人标志着跨大西洋关系的重大转变。 “seismic” 常见的中文释义为 “地震的；影响深远的；重大的”。Open: Pasted image 20250225003042.png
Germany's chancellor-in-waiting didn't wait for the final results of his country's election on Sunday to herald a new era in Europe.“herald” 常见的中文释义为 “预示；宣布；传达”。Declaring the US indifferent to this continent's fate, Friedrich Merz questioned the future of Nato and demanded Europe boost its own defences. Quickly.“indifferent” 的中文意思是 “漠不关心的；冷淡的；不感兴趣的”。This tone from the close US ally - and from Friedrich Merz who is known to be a passionate Atlanticist - would have been unimaginable even a couple of months ago.“passionate” 的中文意思是 “热情的”“充满激情的”It's a seismic shift. That may read like hyperbole, but what we are now experiencing in terms of transatlantic relations is unprecedented in the 80 years since the end of World War Two.hyperbole夸张，夸大其词。 “unprecedented” 的中文意思是 “前所未有的、史无前例的”。Big European powers have been shocked to the core by the Trump administration, which suggests it could revoke the security guarantees to Europe in place since 1945."I would never have thought that I would have to say something like this in a TV show but, after Donald Trump's remarks last week... it is clear that this government does not care much about the fate of Europe," Friedrich Merz said during a post-election debate on Sunday.
Germany's conservatives celebrate, but far right enjoy record result "My absolute priority will be to strengthen Europe as quickly as possible so that, step by step, we can really achieve independence from the USA," he added.Merz hinted that the endeavour was so urgent that he was not sure on whether the transatlantic alliance leaders gathering for a summit in June "would still be talking about Nato in its current form or whether we will have to establish an independent European defence capability much more quickly".“endeavour” 常见的中文释义为 “努力；尽力；尝试”。Significantly, the forthcoming chancellor put Donald Trump's America on a par with Russia - widely viewed here as a security threat to Europe more broadly. "We are under such massive pressure from two sides that my absolute priority now really is to create unity in Europe," Merz said.“par” 在这里的意思是 “同等”“相等”。The UK prime minister heads to Washington on Thursday, following the visit there on Monday by French President Emmanuel Macron.Friedrich Merz admits, indirectly, to a sense of Fomo - fear of missing out. By rights Germany should be there, too, this week, he says. Berlin, is one of Europe's Big Three powers, alongside France and the UK.Fomo 是 “fear of missing out” 的缩写，中文意思为 “害怕错过”。And with the US and Russia now pow-wowing bilaterally, about, but not with, Ukraine, it feels like a global return to big-power politics.“bilaterally” 的中文意思是 “双边地；双方地”。But Germany has been MIA [missing in action] for a good while now on the European and the world stage. The outgoing government here was weakened and distracted by vicious internal bickering. This infuriated German voters - who wanted urgent focus on the economy and migration - and European allies, demanding action on Russia, security and defence.“weakened” 的意思是 “被削弱的”“变弱的”。 “vicious” 在这里的意思是 “恶意的、激烈的、充满敌意的”。 “bickering” 的意思是 “争吵”“口角”“斗嘴”。 “infuriated” 的意思是 “使极为生气”“激怒”。 pow-wowing” 在这里可以理解为 “进行商谈”“举行会谈” 的意思。Merz says a top priority for Germany is to re-engage internationally.The country is already the second-biggest donor of military aid to Ukraine, after the US.Merz wants to continue that support, but, unlike France and the UK, he's been reticent about the idea of sending soldiers to Ukraine, to back up an eventual ceasefire there.“reticent” 的中文意思是 “沉默寡言的；有保留的；不愿多谈的”。Based on Germany's track record though - it dragged its heels at every stage of Ukraine support, and despite that, ended up delivering more aid than any of its European neighbours - a 'No' now, doesn't mean a 'No' forever to committing troops or participating in whatever form a European "reassurance force" in Ukraine may take.“dragged” 在这里的意思是 “拖延”“拖拉”。For now, the soldiers Germans most worry about are the 35,000 American ones, stationed in their country, that make them feel safe.It's highly unusual for foreign policy to be a top voter concern at election time. But in Germany this weekend, alongside the economy and migration, voter after voter said they worried about peace in Europe and felt very insecure.Back in November, Germany's interior ministry said it was drawing up a list of bunkers that could provide emergency shelter for civilians.“interior” 常见的中文释义为 “内部的；国内的；内政的” bunker 的中文意思是 “地堡；掩体；防空洞”。Ukraine may be far away, but Germans feel at great risk from Russia for two reasons.Firstly, the amount of military equipment their country has sent Ukraine. The far right, Alternative for Germany (AfD), with its "Germany First" slogan, campaigned for Berlin to disengage from Kyiv and to re-establish relations with Russia. A strategy not unlike Donald Trump's, as the party is fond of pointing out. “正如该政党喜欢指出的那样。”campaigned” 的中文意思是 “参加活动；进行活动；发起运动”。Secondly, many in Germany think that if Russia wanted to really destabilise Europe, it might be tempted to strike one of the Big Three with a long-range missile.
Open: Pasted image 20250225003133.png
France and the UK are nuclear powers. Germany is not. Even its conventional military is woefully understaffed and underequipped (to the immense irritation of European partners), so Germany fears it's a soft target.法国和英国是核大国。德国不是。甚至德国的常规军事力量严重人手不足且装备不足（这让欧洲伙伴们极为恼火），所以德国担心自己成为一个容易攻击的目标。conventional” 常见的中文释义为 “传统的；常规的；依照惯例的”。 woefully” 的意思是 “很糟糕地；可悲地；不幸地”。All the more so if President Trump withdraws his active servicemen and women from Germany.He has pledged to significantly reduce US troop presence in Europe as a whole.“significantly” 的中文意思是 “显著地、明显地、重大地”。The German sense of deep domestic insecurity prompted【促使；推动；提示】 Friedrich Merz to suggest last week that he'd look to France and Britain to form a European nuclear umbrella, to replace US nuclear guarantees.“domestic” 常见的中文释义为 “国内的；家庭的；家用的”。It's an idea that's easy to bring up on the campaign trail, but that in reality is hugely complex - involving questions of capabilities, commitment and control.这是一个在竞选活动中很容易被提出的想法，但实际上却极其复杂，涉及到能力、承诺和控制等问题。 “involving” 的中文意思是 “涉及”“包含”。 hugely complex极其复杂The reality check: Friedrich Merz will need a lot of money for his plans to secure Germany and Europe, and Germany's economy is depressed.He also has to reach agreement with the coalition partner, or partners, with whom he'll form the next German government - as well as with other European countries, like the UK.“coalition” 的中文意思是 “联合；联盟；结合体”。And they may not want to strike such a strident【尖锐的；刺耳的；强硬的】 tone against the US.This election may herald stronger leadership from Germany. But is the rest of Europe ready?

每日头条/20250225-us-sides-with-russia-in-un.title: 20250225-US sides with Russia in UN resolutions on Ukraine
每日头条/20250225-us-sides-with-russia-in-un.description:
“美国在联合国关于乌克兰的决议中支持俄罗斯”。 “side with” 是一个固定短语，表示 “支持；站在…… 一边”。 Open: Pasted image 20250225234049.png
Watch: US votes against UN resolution condemning Russia aggression against UkraineThe US has twice sided with Russia in votes at the United Nations to mark the third anniversary of the Russian invasion of Ukraine, highlighting the Trump administration's change of stance on the war.“stance” 常见的中文释义为 “立场；态度”。First, the US opposed a European-drafted resolution condemning Moscow's actions and supporting Ukraine's territorial integrity - voting the same way as Russia and countries including North Korea and Belarus at the UN General Assembly (UNGA) in New York.“UN General Assembly” 指联合国大会。Then the US drafted and voted for a resolution at the UN Security Council which called for an end to the conflict, but contained no criticism of Russia.The Security Council passed the resolution, but two key US allies, the UK and France, abstained after their attempts to amend the wording were vetoed.
The UN resolutions were tabled as French President Emmanuel Macron visited President Donald Trump at the White House in an attempt to address their sharp differences over the war.On Thursday, British Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer will likewise visit the new American leader.“likewise” 的中文意思是 “同样地；也；类似地”。Trump's White House has upended the transatlantic alliance, currying favour with Moscow and casting doubt on America's long-term commitment to European security.That rift was laid bare on the floor of the 193-member UNGA on Monday as US diplomats pushed their limited resolution mourning the loss of life during the "Russia-Ukraine conflict" and calling for a swift end to it.周一，这一裂痕在拥有 193 个成员国的联合国大会上暴露无遗，美国外交官推动了他们的有限决议，哀悼 “俄乌冲突” 期间的生命损失，并呼吁迅速结束这场冲突。 “laid” 是动词 “lay” 的过去分词形式。 “mourning” 的中文意思是 “哀悼；服丧”。European diplomats tabled a more detailed text, blaming Russia for its full-scale invasion, and supporting Ukraine's sovereignty and territorial integrity. “sovereignty” 的中文意思是 “主权”"We need to reconfirm that the aggression should be condemned and discredited, not rewarded," said Ukrainian Deputy Foreign Minister Mariana Betsa.UNGA members backed the European resolution by 93 votes but, extraordinarily, the US did not abstain but actually voted against it, along with Russia, Israel, North Korea, Sudan, Belarus, Hungary and 11 other states, with 65 abstentions.“abstain” 在这段文本中的意思是 “弃权”。The UNGA also passed the US resolution but only after it was amended to include language supporting Ukraine, which led to the US abstaining.Republican Senator John Curtis said he was "deeply troubled" by the vote "which put us on the same side as Russia and North Korea".共和党参议员约翰・柯蒂斯说，他对这次投票 “深感不安”，这次投票 “使我们与俄罗斯和朝鲜站在了同一立场”。"These are not our friends. This posture is a dramatic shift from American ideals of freedom and democracy," he wrote on X.The vote was "contrary to our long-standing support of democracy", said former US House of Representatives Speaker Nancy Pelosi.Ukraine's former minister of economy, Tymofiy Mylovanov, said the choice to side with Russia was deliberate.“deliberate” 的中文意思是 “故意的；蓄意的；深思熟虑的”。"This is no longer just rhetoric or political theatre," he said.“这不再仅仅是言辞或政治作秀。” 他说。At the much more powerful 15-member UN Security Council, the unamended US resolution - which called for an end to the conflict but contained no criticism of Russia - was passed by 10 votes, with the UK, France, Denmark, Greece and Slovenia abstaining.America's acting envoy to the UN, Dorothy Camille Shea, described the US resolution as a "simple historic statement... that looks forward, not backwards. A resolution focused on one simple idea: ending the war".Rarely has the US been so at odds with its supposed European allies.“美国很少与其所谓的欧洲盟友如此不和”。 Rarely 的用法：rarely 是一个否定副词，意思是 “很少地，罕见地”。当它位于句首时，句子需要部分倒装，即将助动词、系动词或情态动词提到主语之前，以表示强调或突出否定的意味。 has been 的倒装形式：本句正常语序应该是 “The US has rarely been so at odds with its supposed European allies”。由于 rarely 提前，所以将助动词 has 提到了主语 the US 的前面，形成了 “Rarely has the US...” 的倒装结构。这种倒装主要是为了强调 “rarely” 这一否定概念，突出美国与欧洲盟友如此不和的情况是很少见的。 be at odds with 的用法：这是一个固定短语，意思是 “与…… 不和，与…… 有分歧”，在句中作谓语动词短语，表明美国和其欧洲盟友之间的关系状态。 supposed 的用法：supposed 在这里是一个形容词，意思是 “所谓的，号称的”，用来修饰后面的 “European allies”，带有一种不太认可或怀疑的语气，暗示这些被称作欧洲盟友的国家与美国之间的关系可能并不像表面上那么亲密或稳固。 Since Russia invaded Ukraine three years ago, the Security Council has been deadlocked by the power of Russia, one of its five permanent members, to veto any resolution there.“veto” 在这句话中的意思是 “否决”。For this reason the UNGA has been the main forum for debating the war. But its resolutions are not legally binding for member states, unlike those of the Security Council.

每日头条/20250226-where-is-mr.-musk-in-all-o.title: 20250226-Where is Mr. Musk in all of this？ Judges question secrecy of DOGE's activities
每日头条/20250226-where-is-mr.-musk-in-all-o.description:
“在这一切当中，马斯克先生在哪里？”法官质疑狗狗币活动的保密性。 Open: Pasted image 20250226235437.png
Summary Musk's role in DOGE questioned in court DOGE's secrecy complicates legal challenges Judges have issued mixed rulings on DOGE's access
Feb 26 (Reuters) - On social media and at political rallies, Elon Musk has taken credit for leading the team that is cutting allegedly wasteful U.S. government spending, even waving a chain saw on stage at a conference.“rallies” 常见的中文释义为 “集会”“群众大会” 挥舞着链锯。 “allegedly” 的中文意思是 “据称”“据说”In court, it's a different story.During a hearing on Monday in a case trying to block access by the DOGE cost-cutting team to Treasury Department systems, a federal judge repeatedly pressed a government lawyer to clarify who is running things. "Where is Mr. Musk in all of this?" asked U.S. District Judge Colleen Kollar-Kotelly."I don't have any information beyond close adviser to the president," responded Bradley Humphreys, an attorney for the Department of Justice.attorney 律师"You can't tell me what role he has?" the judge persisted.Kollar-Kotelly did not say if she would block DOGE and Musk from the Treasury Department information systems as requested.Questions about Musk's role and the activities of the team, known as the Department of Government Efficiency, are at the heart of multiple lawsuits seeking to block them from accessing government systems and slashing programs.slashing 大幅削减Many of the suits【案件】 allege【宣称；声称】 that Musk and DOGE are violating【违反；违背】 the Constitution by wielding【行使；运用】 the kind of vast power that only comes from agencies created through the U.S. Congress or appointments made with confirmation by the U.S. Senate.Despite Musk's public assertions【断言；主张；认定】 to the contrary【相反的；对立的】, the Department of Government Efficiency operates in great secrecy.政府效率部在高度保密的状态下运作。The initial executive【行政人员；管理人员；】 orders signed by President Donald Trump setting up DOGE described it primarily as an outfit【装备；服装；机构；组织。】 to modernize software, not an agency. The Trump administration designated Musk a "special government employee."
Musk has been the face of DOGE since its inception【初始；开端；诞生。】, but White House Office of Administration Director Joshua Fisher said in a February 17 court filing【提交文件；备案文件；存档文件】 that Musk is not the outfit's administrator or even a DOGE employee.On Tuesday, the White House identified Amy Gleason as DOGE's "acting administrator." She did not immediately respond to a request for comment made to the Trump administration.The scant information presented in court about who is ordering the cost-cutting and how it is working has led some judges to rule in favor of Musk and DOGE, at least for now. 法庭上关于谁下令削减成本及其运作方式的信息很少，导致一些法官做出有利于马斯克和DOGE的裁决，至少目前是这样。scant【少量的；不足的；欠缺的】 rule in favor of 做出有利于…… 的裁决To block Musk's efforts with a temporary restraining【限制；约束】 order, or TRO, plaintiffs【原告】 must show they will suffer imminent【迫在眉睫】, irreparable【无法弥补的】 harm without one, a high legal bar to clear.很高的法律门槛需要跨越。At a hearing last week in a case brought by unions and Democratic state attorneys general, U.S. District Judge Tanya Chutkan in Washington said DOGE's lack of transparency made it difficult to show it was on the verge【边缘；濒临；即将】 of causing irreparable harm."I don't know if that's deliberate or not, but I will concede【承认；让步；认输】 that it is difficult to see what's happening next and to predict that and come in with a concrete【混凝土；具体的；实在的。】 harm," Chutkan said at the February 17 hearing.The states presented her with extensive【广泛的】 news reporting about DOGE and Musk shuttering【关闭；停止运转；停止活动；】 programs, accessing confidential data, slashing funding and firing personnel【人员；职员；员工】."It's an understatement to say there's a lot of news reports out there," said Chutkan. "But the courts can't act based on the media reports."
She denied a temporary restraining order to prevent DOGE from accessing sensitive information at seven agencies. The case will continue and the attorneys general will seek evidence to support a more permanent injunction【禁令】.In some cases, however, despite noting concerns about DOGE's opacity【不透明度；模糊度；晦涩度】, judges have found there is sufficient evidence to pause its activities.
U.S. District Judge Jeannette Vargas on Friday temporarily blocked DOGE from accessing Treasury systems responsible for trillions of dollars of payments because she found there was a realistic danger that confidential information was going to be disclosed【被披露】.She was particularly troubled that the government did not know what information was accessed by Marko Elez, a former software engineer for Musk's companies who resigned from DOGE on February 6."Even now, weeks after his departure【离开；出发；启程】, the Treasury Department is still reviewing his logs to determine what precisely【精确地；准确地；确切地】 he accessed and what he did with his access," Vargas wrote in her Friday ruling.Government lawyers have even used shifting definitions【不断变化的定义】 for DOGE, which in one instance【例子；实例；事例】 worked in their favor.
U.S. District Judge John Bates in Washington denied a request by the unions for a temporary restraining order against Musk and DOGE.In doing so【在这样做的时候】, Bates noted【注意到 / 已注意到 / 获悉 / 了解到】 that the Trump administration argued【争论；提出理由证明；主张；认为；辩论；表明；说服；争论不休；据理力争；争辩；】 DOGE was an agency in order to comply with a law known as the Economy Act that allowed DOGE to detail its staff to various government agencies. Bates noted特朗普政府辩称 DOGE 是一个机构，以便遵守一项名为《经济法案》的法律，该法律允许 DOGE 将其工作人员分配到各个政府机构。But Trump created DOGE as part of the Executive【行政人员；行政部门；】 Office of the President and therefore not as an agency that is subject to the Freedom of Information Act, an open records law known as FOIA.The judge described DOGE in fairytale terms【童话般的说法 / 术语】: "A Goldilocks entity: not an agency when it is burdensome【繁重的；累赘的；难以承担的。】 but an agency when it is convenient." 一个 “金发姑娘” 实体：当它带来负担时不是一个机构，而当它方便时则是一个机构。“Goldilocks” 常见的中文释义为 “金发姑娘”“金凤花姑娘”。在特定语境中，也可能用来形容 “刚刚好”“不冷不热、不大不小等正合适” 的状态。这里的 “Goldilocks entity” 可以理解为 “刚刚好的实体”，可能是指一种处于某种平衡状态或者具有适度特征的事物。

每日头条/20250302-jeremy-bowen：trump-zelensk.title: 20250302-Jeremy Bowen：Trump-Zelensky row signals looming crisis between Europe and US
每日头条/20250302-jeremy-bowen：trump-zelensk.description:
特朗普与泽连斯基的争执预示着欧美之间迫在眉睫的危机。 Open: Pasted image 20250302230020.png

The relationship between Donald Trump and Volodymyr Zelensky was bad enough before the shouting match in the Oval Office.President Trump had already called him a dictator and said Ukraine started the war - which is a lie.Now the US-Ukraine alliance nurtured by Joe Biden is in pieces.
The public breakdown also signals a major crisis looming between European members of Nato and the US.
There will be many more doubts and questions about the US commitment to European security outside Ukraine. The biggest is whether President Trump would keep the promise his predecessor Harry Truman made in 1949 to treat an attack on a Nato ally as an attack on America.Those concerns are based on what appears to be Trump's determination to restore a strong relationship with Russian President Vladimir Putin.
He has put heavy pressure on Ukraine while offering Putin big concessions - that would have to be made by the Ukrainians.The security of Ukraine is coming a poor second - and Europeans are worrying theirs is too.
President Zelensky's refusal to make those concessions has infuriated Trump.
Follow live reaction and analysis
Steve Rosenberg: Vladimir Putin can afford to sit back and watch events unfold
Ukrainians back Zelensky after disastrous Oval Office encounter
After White House clash, Starmer faces decision about who he can trust
How the Trump-Zelensky talks collapsed in 10 fiery minutes
It's not just the minerals deal that he refused to sign. Ukrainians believe they are in a war for national survival - and that Putin would break any promise to end the war if he is not deterred.That's why Zelensky asked repeatedly for American security guarantees.The meeting ignited into a shouting match after an intervention by Vice-President JD Vance.
There are suspicions now that the public row was - in the words of one diplomatic observer - a planned political mugging: either to force Zelensky to do America's bidding, or to precipitate a crisis that would allow them to blame him for whatever happens next.If Trump follows the breakdown of talks with a freeze on military aid, Ukraine will fight on. The questions are how effectively, and for how long.
Pressure will redouble on its European allies to take up the slack.

每日头条/20250303-zelensky,-trump-and-europe.title: 20250303-Zelensky, Trump and Europe： Where does a weekend of frantic talks leave them
每日头条/20250303-zelensky,-trump-and-europe.description:
泽连斯基、特朗普和欧洲：一场疯狂的周末会谈将把他们带向何方？ frantic

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky is back in Kyiv after three frantic days - which began with him being ordered to leave the White House following a tense and public showdown with Donald Trump and JD Vance on Friday.
He found a warmer welcome in London on the weekend, where he was greeted by the prime minister outside Downing Street, visited the King, and received a strong show of support from European leaders at a summit on Sunday - a sharp contrast to the scenes in the Oval Office.
After the London summit, Sir Keir Starmer suggested European leaders would form a "coalition of the willing" to defend Ukraine - but details of who would contribute what were scarce.Here's the latest on Zelensky's relationship with Trump, and Europe's plans to guarantee Ukraine's security.
Zelensky, Trump and Europe - follow live updates
Watch: From laughter to anger, how the Oval Office meeting spiralledIn a series of social media posts on Saturday morning, President Zelensky said Ukraine and the US needed to be "honest and direct with each other" to understand their shared goals - and he wanted America to "stand more firmly" on their side.
Appearing on Fox News hours after leaving the White House, Zelensky said the confrontation was a "really tough situation" and took the chance to thank Americans and Donald Trump. He also stopped short of an outright apology despite calls from US lawmakers for him to do so.While Trump hasn't commented directly on the angry exchange over the weekend, most Republican figures have expressed their support for Trump and Vance.National Security Adviser Mike Waltz - who was in the Oval Office during Friday's heated meeting - compared the Ukrainian leader to an "ex-girlfriend", while Speaker Mike Johnson called for Zelensky to quit.
However, moderate Republican Nebraska Congressman Don Bacon said it was "a bad day for America's foreign policy" and Alaska Senator Lisa Murkowski said she is "sick to my stomach as the administration appears to be walking away from our allies and embracing Putin".
Vance took the lead attacking Zelensky. Why?
Was Starmer's summit enough to sway Trump?
Posts on social media in support of Zelensky poured in shortly after he left the White House on Friday evening. Among the notable exceptions were Italy's Giorgia Meloni, who wants to preserve her excellent relations with the Trump administration, and Hungary's Viktor Orban, who praised Donald Trump for "standing bravely for peace".
By the time the London summit came around on Sunday, there was a sense that concrete action had to follow words of support – with most leaders careful to highlight that they still considered US support essential.At the end of the summit, Starmer outlined a four-point plan for peace which included the continuation of military aid to Ukraine, a commitment for Ukraine to be present at peace talks, boosting Ukraine's defence capabilities to deter future Russian aggression, and developing a "coalition of the willing" to defend Ukraine, including sending troops to Ukraine.Starmer said that the idea of sending troops to Ukraine - which would include boots on the ground and planes in the air - had the backing of several parties, but he was careful to leave it to individual countries to discuss the matter internally.Scandinavian countries have already signalled they would be open to the idea. Denmark's Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen said she was keeping an "open mind" on the proposal, while Sweden's Ulf Kristersson said his country was ready to provide Ukraine with security guarantees – if it had the backing of the US.
Italy's Giorgia Meloni would much rather push for another summit that includes the US than discuss a European contingent in Ukraine – a possibility which she says "perplexes" her.
And Poland – which has long been one of Kyiv's most vocal supporters – has already ruled out sending soldiers, although it put few boundaries on humanitarian and military aid to Ukraine.European leaders will now have a few days to digest the latest developments before they meet again in Brussels on Thursday for a special meeting on defence, at which Commission chief Ursula von der Leyen will present what she has called "a comprehensive plan on how to rearm Europe".“UK plays down Macron's truce plan” 的意思是 “英国淡化马克龙的休战计划”。
具体来说，“UK” 指的是 “英国”；“plays down” 表示 “淡化、贬低、对…… 轻描淡写”；“Macron's” 是 “马克龙的”；“truce plan” 即 “休战计划”。这句话可能出现在国际新闻报道中，描述英国对法国总统马克龙提出的某个休战计划持不太重视或不太积极的态度。
EPAEmmanuel Macron, Sir Keir Starmer and Volodymyr Zelenskiy attend the European leaders' summit at Lancaster House in London to discuss security
On Sunday night, the French newspaper Le Figaro reported that President Emmanuel Macron and Starmer have proposed a potential one-month truce between Russia and Ukraine, "in the air and at sea".
Details of any agreement are scarce and the idea put forward by the French remains just that. Under the hypothesis, both sides would agree a truce for four weeks in the air, on the sea and around energy infrastructure. But, Macron has suggested it would not cover fighting on the ground along the front line, as it would be too hard to monitor.But on Monday morning, the UK's armed forces minister played down the idea of a truce insisting that "no agreement has been made on what a truce looks like".
Luke Pollard told Times Radio: "We are working together with France and our European allies to look at what is the path to how... we create a lasting and durable peace in Ukraine."Any truce would have to be agreed by Russia and there is no evidence yet they are willing to do that.
Getty Images
Over the weekend Maria Zakharova claimed Zelensky is "obsessed" with prolonging the warAlthough Vladimir Putin has not yet officially commented on the Washington encounter, the Kremlin's foreign ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova said it had been a "complete diplomatic failure of Kyiv".On Monday morning, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov then added his criticism of the London summit on Ukraine."Statements were made there about the need to step up funding for Ukraine as a matter of urgency. This is obviously not part of a peace plan but is done to continue the fighting," Peskov said.Statements were made there about the need to step up funding for Ukraine as a matter of urgency 那里有人发表声明，表示迫切需要增加对乌克兰的资金支持。
"The rest will depend on what kind of peace plans will be drawn up and offered for discussion. Any constructive support for this process would be welcome now, and any constructive initiatives."
Remarking on the response to the war more broadly, Peskov also suggested that "the collective West has partially begun to lose its collectivity".`` Remarking on the response to the war more broadly, Peskov also suggested that "the collective West has partially begun to lose its collectivity".更广泛地评论对战争的反应时，佩斯科夫还表示，“西方集体在一定程度上已经开始失去其集体性”。

每日头条/20250304-china-retaliates-against-u.title: 20250304-China retaliates against US tariffs - but it also wants to talk
每日头条/20250304-china-retaliates-against-u.description:
中国对美国的关税进行了报复，但同时也希望进行对话。"China will fight to the bitter end of any trade war," the foreign ministry spokesperson in Beijing declared, after China announced tit-for-tat tariffs on agricultural imports from the US.This came within minutes of a new 10% US levy on Chinese imports that came into effect on Tuesday - which adds to existing tariffs both from Trump's first term and those announced last month.But China's latest retaliatory measures are an opening swing, not a direct punch.It shows some strength, and it has the potential to sting parts of the United States, but also leaves room to negotiate or escalate if necessary."We advise the US to put away it's bullying face and return to the right track of dialogue and co-operation before it is too late," foreign ministry spokesperson Lin Jian added.This is the second round of tariffs the two countries have imposed on each other since February. But this time China is hitting Donald Trump where it has the potential to hurt - by targeting farmers, who are some of his core supporters.Almost 78% of farming-dependent counties in the US endorsed Mr Trump in 2024.China is one of their biggest customers for produce such as chicken, beef, pork and soybeans and now all those products will face a 10-15% tax which will come into effect on 10 March."The tariffs are broadly negative for US agricultural markets. It is going to have a bearish influence on prices. There are enough corn and soybean supplies in the world for China to make a switch, it is more of an issue for the US, because 30% of US soybeans still go to China," Ole Houe, of Ikon commodities, told Reuters news agency.Beijing may hope that this will apply some pressure on the Trump administration ahead of any potential negotiations.The latest announcements raise the prospect of an all-out trade war between the world's top two economies and in various ministry statements, China is making two things very clear.Firstly, it is prepared to continue to fight."Pressure, coercion and threats are not the right way to deal with the Chinese side," said Mr Lin.But secondly, it is also willing to talk.Beijing is not ramping up the rhetoric or the tariffs in the same way it did in 2018, during the last Trump administration. Back then it imposed a tariff of 25% on US soybeans."China's tariffs impact a limited number of US products, and remain below the 20% level. This is by design. China's government is signalling that they do not want to escalate, they want to de-escalate," according to Even Pay, an analyst with Trivium China.The prospect of talks was raised last month.The White House said there would be a call between President Xi and Donald Trump. That never happened.So will these talks take place and who will make the first move?
A new 10% US levy on Chinese imports that came into effect on Tuesday is likely to hurt BeijingChina is unlikely to want to go first. It will not want to be seen kowtowing to Washington.And in contrast to Canada and Mexico, Beijing has not announced new measures to target the flow of fentanyl. It simply repeated past statements that fentanyl is a "US problem" and that China has the strictest drug policies in the world.On Tuesday, the State Council released a White Paper entitled "Controlling Fentanyl-related substances - China's contribution."It outlines the measures Beijing says it has already made to crack down on Fentanyl-related crimes and the precursor chemicals used to make the drug. It adds that it is "diligently fulfilling international drug control obligations".So, while China hasn't picked up the phone to Washington, this document forms part of the country's message which appears to be saying - we are already doing what we can on fentanyl.Despite stating that China "will not yield", these latest tariffs are bound to sting.The cumulative 20% tax on all Chinese goods comes on top of a slew of tariffs Trump imposed in his first term on tens of billions of dollars of Chinese imports. And China's population is already concerned about a sluggish economy.Thousands of delegates are gathering in the capital this week to take part in an annual parliamentary session, most of which will focus on the economy.House prices are still falling, and youth unemployment remains stubbornly high. A potential trade war with the US could prompt more money worries for businesses and consumers across the country at a time when the Communist Party wants people to spend to help the economy to grow.
But Beijing will also see an opportunity as Donald Trump sows uncertainty among his international allies.It can partly place the blame for any further economic woes at Washington's door and state that it's the fault of the US for starting a trade war.The state media outlet Xinhua has in recent days released a series of parodies poking fun at a United States that is prepared to tax its allies and neighbours. The skits portray Washington as a bully echoing the words coming from the leaders of Canada and Mexico.At the same time, China's Commerce Ministry has reiterated that it is prepared to work with other countries around the world to combat Mr Trump's tariffs.Beijing appears to be looking for potential allies in this trade war while also trying to cast Washington as a troublemaker who is prepared to target friends and foes alike.All at a time when Donald Trump's 'America First' doctrine has many in Europe and the UK wondering if the US-led world order is already in doubt.
